why: The second artifact of the aetheris-core-v1 architecture, and the first trained on an assembled corpus rather than on this repository's text alone. Recorded here so the preset in services/core/src/klyvaron/architecture.mjs can be checked against the run instead of asserted.
command: python3 -u services/fabric/scripts/train_lm.py --corpus-root artifacts/corpus --extensions .py,.pyi,.md,.rst,.txt,.js,.json,.ts --validation-sources pallets__click,psf__requests --run-name klyvaron-mini-lm --d-model 192 --n-layers 3 --n-heads 4 --d-ff 768 --seq-len 128 --batch-size 16 --steps 4000 --warmup-steps 200 --output-dir artifacts --json artifacts/klyvaron-mini-lm.report.json

outcome.verdict: RELEASED by the family's own gate: 0 hard failures, 1 soft failure (wallSeconds 8456.326 against a 3600 s soft target, recorded on the card rather than waived)
outcome.note: Every number here was read out of the run's own report; none of them was typed before the run finished. The report is gitignored (it embeds the weights digest and the full per-file corpus manifest) and is reproduced by the command above.

sizing.measuredAt: 2026-10-15, this host, 2 CPU cores, measured from the run's own log rather than from a scaled estimate. Step 1 printed at 16:55:36, step 401 at 17:22:27 (1,611 s for 400 steps, 4.03 s/step -- this interval had this repository's test suites and some profiling running beside it), step 801 at 17:35:04 (757 s for the next 400 steps, 1.89 s/step, which is what the run does when it has the machine mostly to itself). An earlier 0.70 s/step figure here was scaled from a 20-step measurement at d160 and was wrong by a factor of three.
sizing.projected: 3,200 steps remaining at about 1.9 s/step is about 1.7 h, plus about 270 s of fixed cost (tokenizer, baselines, full held-out evaluation): the run finishes around 19:20 on the day it started.
sizing.why: The size is what a single sitting on this machine can train to a demonstrated loss, and it is small enough that the whole recipe -- corpus, tokenizer, config, training, evaluation, release -- completes in one go rather than being planned.

retention.observed: The run wrote its weights, report and corpus snapshot into artifacts/ and hashed them there -- the filename, byte count and digests in `outcome.artifact` were read off the files that existed at 19:16 on 2026-10-15. That directory is gitignored by policy (weights are referenced by digest, never redistributed through Git), and it is not carried by this workspace's snapshots either: on 2026-10-16 `artifacts/` is absent, and `find / -name 'klyvaron-mini-lm*'` returns only the three records in docs/.
retention.consequence: The digests are therefore the whole of what remains of the run's output. The command above rebuilds an artifact of this kind in about 2.4 h; it does not rebuild these bytes, and after the fix described in `provenanceNote` it would not even rebuild this corpus -- see below.

provenanceNote.why: `scripts/assemble_corpus.py` copies this repository's own text off the working tree while recording only `git rev-parse HEAD`, and truncates each source at a byte cap in sorted-path order. The tree it read on 2026-10-15 had 45 uncommitted paths in it, so the revision it recorded (`e616bdc9863fa92588b389f7ff5ba0dc3a5dda6e`) does not describe the bytes that were copied, and the cap makes the file set depend on the tree's shape at that moment. The manifest digest f8dfef6f is a record of what was read, not a recipe.
provenanceNote.fixed: The assembler now records `clean` and a `treeDigest` over the path and content of every file copied, and marks the revision `-dirty` when the tree does not match it -- the same suffix `train.code_revision()` has always written for the code revision. `services/fabric/tests/test_corpus_assembly.py` covers both, including that the two definitions agree. This record's own `corpus.sourcesRecord` predates the fix, so its first-party entry names the commit without that suffix.
